articles.title: Semiconductor Boom Turns Korean Chip-Equipment Founder Into A Billionaire - Yahoo Finance
articles.summary: Semiconductor Boom Turns Korean Chip-Equipment Founder Into A Billionaire  Yahoo Finance
articles.full_text:
The AI-driven memory boom has turned Park Kyoung-soo, founder of PSK Holdings, into a billionaire. Shares of the South Korean chip-equipment maker, which trades on South Korea's tech-focused Kosdaq exchange, surged more than threefold over the past year. Park, 73, who owns roughly 35% of PSK Holdings, including shares held by his three daughters, is the company's largest shareholder. Based on that stake, Forbes estimates his net worth at $1.1 billion at Thursday's market close.
Based in Hwaseong, south of Seoul and near Samsung Electronics' semiconductor factories, PSK Holdings makes machines that clean and connect the components inside high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and other advanced semiconductor packages. These packages place AI processors close to stacks of HBM, allowing data to move rapidly between the processor and memory. In the first half of this year, revenue rose 14% year over year to 75.3 billion won ($55 million), while net income climbed 35% to 44 billion won.
One of its main products, Ecolite, uses plasma to remove microscopic residue left behind when chipmakers use a light-sensitive material called photoresist to create redistribution layers, which are microscopic copper wires that carry electrical signals between chips and other components inside the package. Another main product, Geneva, melts tiny pieces of solder that electrically connect one chip or layer to another—a critical step in assembling packages that combine AI processors with stacks of HBM.
Analysts at KB Securities said in a July research note that they expect demand for Ecolite to grow as memory chip makers such as Samsung, SK hynix and Micron expand HBM production to supply AI accelerators, which need HBM's faster data-transfer speeds to keep their processors supplied with data. The analysts also expect demand for Geneva to grow because chipmakers are expanding production capacity for advanced packages that use the equipment to form electrical connections between AI processors, HBM and the layers beneath them.
Park founded PSK Holdings in 1990 and took it public on the Kosdaq in 1997. Before starting the company, Park worked for Miryung Construction, founded by fellow billionaire Kim Jun-ki, which is now known as DB Construction. There, he worked on the construction of a silicon-wafer factory for U.S. seeds and pesticides maker Monsanto, whose electronic-materials division manufactured silicon wafers for chip makers at the time. He has a bachelor's degree in business from Korea University in Seoul and an M.B.A. from California State University, Los Angeles.

articles.title: Korea Alcohol Group Shifts From Ethanol to Semiconductor Materials Value Chain - thelec.net
articles.summary: Korea Alcohol Group Shifts From Ethanol to Semiconductor Materials Value Chain  thelec.net
articles.full_text:
Korea Alcohol Group is shifting its portfolio toward semiconductor materials, moving the focus from ethanol and commodity chemicals to higher-value semiconductor materials. The group has built a circular semiconductor materials value chain connecting its affiliates, covering the process from production and distribution to resource recycling. It is also establishing a production hub in Yesan, South Chungcheong Province, bringing together major materials affiliates.
According to industry sources on Oct. 1, Korea Alcohol Group has expanded its semiconductor materials business through affiliates including KC&A, Korea Alcohol Industrial, ENF Technology, UBM, PURIT and PAM Technology. The growing share of high-value semiconductor products has translated into improved earnings.
Korea Alcohol Industrial's standalone sales in the first half of this year rose 8.6% from a year earlier to 153.2 billion won. Operating profit increased 123% to 13.6 billion won. PURIT reported sales of 82.6 billion won and operating profit of 12.5 billion won, up 19.3% and 64.8%, respectively. ENF Technology reported consolidated sales of 349.9 billion won and operating profit of 52.2 billion won, increases of 8.7% and 16%, respectively.
Korea Alcohol Industrial is the only company in South Korea producing normal butyl acetate, according to the company. It began as an ethanol producer in 1984 and entered the electronic materials market in 1999 after completing an electronic-grade normal butyl acetate plant in Ulsan. Normal butyl acetate is an organic solvent used to control the dissolution performance and volatility of semiconductor thinners. Thinners are solvents used in semiconductor photolithography to dilute photoresist (PR) or remove residual PR from the edge of wafers. Korea Alcohol Industrial's official materials identify normal butyl acetate and electronic and semiconductor materials among its businesses.
PURIT, established in 2010 to recover and refine waste organic solvents, has expanded its portfolio into high-purity chemicals for semiconductors. It currently produces high-purity organic solvents used in semiconductor photolithography, including propylene glycol monomethyl ether (PGME), propylene glycol monomethyl ether acetate (PGMEA), ethyl 3-ethoxypropionate (EEP) and ethyl lactate (EL).
Among these products, PGME and PGMEA are supplied as raw materials for semiconductor thinners and other products manufactured by ENF Technology. EEP is supplied to Dow Chemical and Dongjin Semichem, while EL is supplied to Dongjin Semichem and others. Semiconductor materials accounted for more than 80% of PURIT's sales in the first half of this year, at 66.8 billion won.
ENF Technology has also shifted its focus from displays to semiconductor materials. Semiconductor materials sales began surpassing display materials in 2020. They now account for about 65% of total semiconductor-related sales. The company supplies thinners, etchants, strippers, cleaning solutions, monomers and polymers used in semiconductor photolithography and etching processes. Semiconductor materials sales have recently increased, led by hydrofluoric acid (HF)-based etchants that the company has successfully localized. ENF Technology's official materials describe its portfolio as including process chemicals for semiconductor and display manufacturing.
The group has also expanded its product portfolio by adding affiliates. In 2021, ENF Technology acquired a stake in UBM to enter the chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) slurry market. CMP slurry is a material made by mixing abrasive particles and chemicals used for wafer planarization. Earlier this year, ENF Technology increased its stake in PAM Technology, a joint venture with Japan's Morita Chemical Industries, making it a consolidated subsidiary. PAM Technology produces hydrofluoric acid-based buffered oxide etchant (BOE) and ammonia water, a raw material. ENF Technology's official materials identify UBM as a semiconductor CMP slurry company and PAM Technology as a producer of HF/BOE etchants.
The group has established a structure linking the businesses of its affiliates from raw-material sourcing and distribution through basic chemical materials, advanced semiconductor materials, and recycling and resource circulation. KC&A sources chemical raw materials in South Korea and overseas, while Korea Alcohol Industrial and PURIT produce high-purity electronic-grade solvents. ENF Technology uses those materials to make semiconductor process products such as thinners. PURIT also operates a waste organic-solvent recycling business using waste generated during manufacturing processes. KC&A describes its role as supplying raw materials to affiliates including Korea Alcohol Industrial and ENF Technology.
The group is also building a large production hub bringing together its major materials affiliates. Korea Alcohol Industrial, ENF Technology and PURIT are establishing an integrated campus in the Yesan 2 General Industrial Complex in South Chungcheong Province, with a combined investment of 450 billion won. PURIT has moved fastest on construction. It plans to invest about 45 billion won and complete preparations for production in the first half of 2027. The investment could be increased to as much as 100 billion won depending on future demand. Korea Alcohol Industrial and ENF Technology have secured sites with investments of 14.3 billion won and 31.8 billion won, respectively.
The group plans to continue expanding each affiliate's business around semiconductor materials. Korea Alcohol Industrial has set a target of 805 billion won in consolidated sales, 88.2 billion won in operating profit and a return on equity (ROE) of at least 12% by 2030.

articles.title: Micron Posts Record Results on AI Demand as Korea, Japan Fund U.S. Power Plants - en.sedaily.com
articles.summary: Micron Posts Record Results on AI Demand as Korea, Japan Fund U.S. Power Plants  en.sedaily.com
articles.full_text:
Global Morning Briefing is a roundup of worldwide news compiled by Seoul Economic Daily.
Micron's AI Data Center Revenue Jumps 11-Fold; 35% of Four-Year Sales Already Locked In
Micron Technology, the U.S. memory chipmaker often seen as a barometer for the semiconductor market, posted record results for both the quarter and the full year. Revenue from its data center business surged 11-fold in a single year on artificial intelligence demand. By shrugging off concerns that the cycle had peaked and confirming the memory upcycle, the results are raising expectations that favorable conditions will extend to earnings at Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and SK hynix (000660.KS).
Micron said in a filing that revenue reached a record $54.23 billion (about 73.704 trillion won) in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, which ran from May 29 to Sept. 3. It marked the sixth straight quarter of record revenue.
Quarterly revenue rose nearly fivefold from $11.32 billion a year earlier, beating the $51.07 billion average estimate compiled by the London Stock Exchange Group. Annual revenue also hit a record, jumping 256% to $133.19 billion from $37.38 billion a year earlier.
Adjusted earnings per share for the fourth quarter came in at $33.42, above the $31.61 estimate. Micron said it expects first-quarter revenue of $61.5 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $38.15 in fiscal 2027, higher than LSEG estimates of $57 billion and $35.40.
Chief Executive Sanjay Mehrotra said the company is gaining confidence that strategic customer agreements will make its financial performance more robust. Under the arrangements, customers commit in advance to specific memory volumes and amounts.
Trump Uses Allied Money to Clear the AI Bottleneck
Investment projects in the United States that South Korea, Japan and others have finalized with the Trump administration share a common feature: they are concentrated on power plant construction. Most of the selected sites are places where data centers, the core infrastructure for AI, already operate at scale or are slated for construction. That has led to analysis that Washington is using allied investment as leverage to resolve the electricity constraints that have emerged as a bottleneck for advanced industries.
Pennsylvania, where the United States and Japan agreed in March to spend $17 billion on a 4.3-gigawatt natural gas power plant, is a region where AI power demand is rising sharply. It is also where Amazon said last year it would invest at least $20 billion to build an AI and cloud data center campus.
Texas, where both South Korea and Japan plan to build gas-fired power plants, is one of the world's most closely watched data center hubs.
Citadel Securities said in a recent report that China will add nearly six times more generation capacity than the United States over the next five years, while the United States will struggle with grid interconnection, permitting procedures and local opposition to data centers.
Passengers Avert Airliner Crash After Co-Pilot Stabs Captain
Attention is focused on the motive behind an incident in which a co-pilot stabbed the captain on a flight bound for Israel, nearly causing the aircraft to crash. With the exact motive still unestablished, Israeli officials appear to be leaning toward the possibility of terrorism driven by religious extremism.
On the 30th, a co-pilot of Omani nationality attacked the Indian captain with a bladed weapon aboard a Flydubai Boeing 737 MAX flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv. There were 174 passengers on board, 166 of them Israelis. The aircraft plunged from 34,000 feet to 17,000 feet in less than a minute. The seriously wounded captain opened the cockpit door, and three Israeli passengers and a crew member entered and subdued the co-pilot. Two off-duty pilots traveling as passengers then took over the controls and made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, averting a major disaster.
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz described the incident as an attempted jihadist terror attack, saying initial information indicated the attacker had only one intention: to crash the aircraft with everyone on board.
In an interview with Fox News, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the exact background was unclear but that the man clearly hated Israelis. Asked whether there were signs that Iran was involved, he said it was too early to say.
Full Pay Past Retirement Age: Japan Courts Older Workers
Japanese companies have long cut wages by about half when rehiring workers past the mandatory retirement age, but going forward they must pay the full amount unless there is a clear reason not to. That is because workers rehired after retirement have been brought under the scope of equal pay for equal work. It is a stopgap measure devised by Japan, which unlike South Korea faces labor shortages extending even to older workers.
According to the Nihon Keizai Shimbun on the 1st, the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare put revised equal pay for equal work guidelines, amended in April, into effect that day. The revision allows non-regular workers to demand that employers explain why their treatment differs from that of permanent employees doing the same work. Employers must also set standards for allowances, leave and benefits.
The revised guidelines also bar employers from differentiating treatment for older workers hired on fixed-term contracts after retirement, known as shokutaku staff, solely on the grounds that they have been switched to contract status. Last year, Japan had a record 9.43 million workers aged 65 and over, 76.1% of whom were non-regular workers, meaning they fall under the new rules.
Japan has been pushing back retirement ages since 2005, when it became the world's first country in which people aged 65 and over exceeded 20% of the total population, making it a super-aged society.
Paramount-Warner Merger Settlement Reached With 150-Film Production Condition
Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery has cleared its last major hurdle. With an antitrust lawsuit filed by 12 states resolved through a settlement in U.S. federal court, the merger is expected to close soon.
According to The Wall Street Journal on the 30th, the federal court approved a settlement between the two sides in an antitrust suit brought against Paramount by the attorneys general of 12 states, led by California. Because the European Union granted conditional approval of the merger in July, the U.S. federal ruling was the final gateway for the deal. Paramount said it expects the transaction to close on Oct. 6 following the decision.
The two companies agreed to establish an editorial board of five journalists within 180 days of completing the merger. The board will have authority to mediate disputes among CBS News and CNN staff over violations of editorial principles, reporting bias, fairness and related issues.

articles.title: ​Applied Materials, Besi to Co-Develop Hybrid Bonding at EPIC Center - thelec.net
articles.summary: ​Applied Materials, Besi to Co-Develop Hybrid Bonding at EPIC Center  thelec.net
articles.full_text:
Applied Materials and BE Semiconductor Industries NV, known as Besi, are expanding their collaboration on next-generation packaging technologies including heterogeneous integration and bonding.
THE ELEC reported on October 1 that Besi will join Applied Materials' EPIC Center as an innovation partner. The EPIC Center, short for Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization, is a collaborative research and development facility being established in Silicon Valley for semiconductor equipment and process innovation. It aims to significantly shorten the time required to commercialize technologies developed by semiconductor companies, from research to high-volume manufacturing.
Engineers from the two companies will jointly develop full-flow solutions for advanced packaging technologies ranging from wafer-level packaging (WLP) to panel-level packaging (PLP) at the EPIC Center. Demand for chip-to-chip and chip-to-package integration with higher density and bandwidth has increased as companies accelerate the build-out of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.
The companies will focus on 3D integrated circuits (ICs) for next-generation AI compute and memory architectures, as well as logic-memory integration. The work will include developing new die-to-wafer (D2W) hybrid bonding equipment, expanding thermo-compression bonding (TCB) technology and building an ecosystem spanning front-end and back-end processes. It will also cover die-on-wafer (DoW) process technology and equipment platforms, die-on-die (DoD) platforms, die-on-panel (DoP) integrated platforms and co-packaged optics (CPO) interconnect technology.
D2W hybrid bonding is an advanced packaging technology that directly bonds dies, or chips, to wafers using copper and dielectric materials. Unlike conventional TCB, it does not use a soldering process in which metal bumps, or microbumps, are melted to connect chips. The technology increases signal transmission speeds and reduces power consumption, making it a key technology for high-performance AI computing.
DoW places individual dies on a wafer and bonds them, while DoD directly stacks and bonds another die vertically on an individual die that has already been cut from a wafer. DoP places multiple chips across a large square panel, such as a glass substrate, and packages them simultaneously. CPO is a next-generation packaging technology that integrates optical chips, including silicon photonics devices that transmit signals using light, with high-performance electronic chips in a single package.
Advanced packaging was historically treated as a simple assembly step in the back-end process. In contrast, next-generation technologies such as hybrid bonding and PLP require materials engineering capabilities, high precision and cleanliness comparable to those used in front-end wafer manufacturing.
The two companies began collaborating in 2020, when they established a joint center at Applied Materials’ Advanced Packaging Development Center in Singapore. The collaboration combined Applied Materials’ advanced semiconductor process technologies, including etch, planarization, deposition, cleaning and precision metrology, with Besi’s die placement, interconnect and assembly technologies. The result was the launch last year of Kinex, the industry’s first integrated D2W hybrid bonding system, according to Applied Materials.
More than 10 companies and institutions, including Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, Micron Technology, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) and Broadcom, are participating in the EPIC Center. The center is in the final stages of preparations for operation. Research and development equipment is being moved into its clean rooms, and a center unveiling ceremony is scheduled for Oct. 12. A total investment of $5 billion is planned for the center.
